Candidate causes include: oxygen loss or Sr segregation in UHV; cleave-induced strain or microcracking; local over-doping (the authors' own fits reach p ≈ 0.3, beyond the LSCO superconducting dome)
At the more overdoped x = 0.22, the gap should be smaller still. It would then be comparable to the 3–4 meV resolution plus thermal and kz broadening.
There are no XPS core-level data (Cu 2p satellite structure, O 1s, La/Sr ratio). There is no LEED or cross-sectional TEM, so surface order and stoichiometry are undetermined.

notes: C10 is explicitly raised in Section 4(3) of the review ('Map flat-band peak visibility versus disorder strength, correlation length, and type'), which corresponds to the disorder-scale and single-model critiques summarized in P13 and P20. C5 and C6 are judged 'partly' because the review notes that kz broadening/smearing is comparable to the expected gap and inconsistently reported (0.2 vs 0.4 A^-1), without explicitly spelling out near-nodal momentum mixing into the antinodal cut.
